correctness.rationale: Dihedral averaging reduces the global SLEM value to the two-orbit family with p+2q≤1, not the set of all optimizers. The first Fourier block gives the lower bound 1−p−qt+sqrt(p²+q²t²) at t=1−cos(2π/n). It decreases strictly in q when p>0; p=0 has a unit eigenvalue on the nonconstant subspace. On q=(1−p)/2 the bound is strictly convex in p, with second derivative a²/(p²+a²(1−p)²)^(3/2)>0 for a=t/2. At the claimed p and q the square root is x/2 and the scalar derivative vanishes, verifying the interior minimum. The plus branches decrease with t_k, and the minus branches are bounded below by −sqrt(p²+(1−p)²) at t_k=2. The difference of squares from the claimed SLEM is x(x+2)(2−x²)/D²>0 since x²≤3/2, including the triangle boundary. The nonconstant k=0 eigenvalue (2−x²)/D is also strictly below the SLEM. Thus the lower bound is attained, and both equality conditions prove invariant uniqueness. The exact gap x²/D∼π²/n² gives the claimed factor 1/2 against the bare cycle.
residual_risks: The phrase ‘nonsymmetric chains’ in the finding does not widen the feasible class; stochastic matrices remain symmetric and the unclassified multiplicity is for non-dihedrally-invariant competitors.

evidence: The 9e788ca7bde4 theorem applies to vertex- and edge-transitive regular cores. Take a degree-two cycle core with one leaf per vertex and use spectral parameter a=1−cos(2π/n)=x². It gives D=1+(1+x)², the stated edge weights, SLEM 1−x²/D and zero rim holding. The 4/5 barrier is exact for C_4=K_{2,2} only in the noncomplete cycle family, not for general n.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Every cycle including C_3 satisfies the broader exact theorem's core assumptions. The wheel, bare cycle, and non-sharp barrier do not give this specialization.
